data.title: Flex
data.tagline: Arrange items along one row or one column
data.description: Flexbox lays items out on a single main axis and handles alignment, spacing, wrapping, and flexible size. It is a good fit for toolbars, form rows, and card content. Use Grid when both rows and columns need a planned structure.

use: Let items wrap when room runs out
avoid: Use many nested flex containers for a simple grid
Set fixed widths that fight the flexible layout
Forget how the order changes on small screens
Use visual order that differs from keyboard and reading order

lessonPractice.title: A toolbar has one row: a title on the left and a changing number of actions on the right, all vertically centered. Which layout is most direct?

options.label: Absolutely position the actions on the right and tune each top value
options.feedback: Removing actions from normal flow makes overlap likely when the title or action count changes.

options.label: Use Flex on the parent, distribute both sides, and center the cross axis
options.feedback: This is a one-axis relationship. Flex keeps the two groups at opposite ends and aligns them vertically.

options.label: Give the title and every action fixed margins until they reach the target positions
options.feedback: Fixed distances only fit the current content and stop preserving the relationship when text or actions change.

data.agentPrompt: Use Flex for the toolbar with the title on the left, actions on the right, and vertical centering. Preserve that relationship as actions change, and allow sensible wrapping when narrow. Do not force placement with absolute positioning or fixed margins.

references.title: A Complete Guide to CSS Flexbox
